entities.summary: William de la Marck (1446–1485) was an adventurer of German extraction. He became an important character in the late 15th century in the Prince-Bishopric of Liège. William's was nicknamed Le Sanglier des Ardennes — because he was as fierce as the wild boar which he delighted to hunt.
